summary.name: Quarters
summary.one_liner: Quarters is a free, open-source workspace for running terminal coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI across many projects at once, with a Mac app and a remote browser or phone view.
use_cases: run several coding agents in different projects at once
start a whole dev stack with one click
get notified when an agent is waiting for input
approve or steer an agent from a phone or tablet
undo a bad agent turn with file checkpoints
search all projects' code at once
summary.what_it_does: Quarters gives each project its own room with terminals, where you can run Claude Code or another supported coding agent, switch projects with one click or ⌘P, and see which agent is waiting for you. Automations open a set of terminals with their own folders and commands, such as a backend, frontend and a script, in one action. It includes split panes, a file browser with a simple editor, git commit/push and pull request check views, per-prompt file checkpoints you can restore, and a search across all projects. A remote access mode serves the same live sessions to a browser, including phones, from the machine that holds the code.
notable: Works with many agents: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Aider, OpenCode, Goose, Amp and others, with Claude Code getting the deepest view
Remote access from any browser or phone, with passkeys and the server only listening on the host machine
Per-prompt git-based checkpoints kept off every branch so git push never sends them
Installs via Homebrew cask; MIT licensed with no telemetry or account
caveats: You must have the coding agent you use installed and signed in separately
Linux runs only as a server; Windows is client-only via a browser
Not an IDE; the file editor is intentionally minimal
Remote access needs a tunnel you set up (such as Cloudflare or Tailscale) or home Wi-Fi
